mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in PARKS together with persistently negative WORKPLACES signals more discretionary movement and shorter daytime trips, which should spill into higher retail visitation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS remains above baseline or rises while WORKPLACES stays depressed and RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week average within 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM indicates precautionary, necessity-only trip behavior that substitutes away from discretionary shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next one to two weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above its current level but RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the last week within 7-14 days, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT drops further below -15 percent, reduced access to central retail zones suppresses shopping trips and keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -15 after having been above -15 in the prior week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses below -15 and RETAIL_REC does not decline versus the previous four-week mean within 28 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increases weekday city-center circulation, which should lift retail-and-recreation mobility after a two-week lag.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A return of PARKS activity above baseline during autumn weekends signals favorable weather and leisure demand, which should support retail outings over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 0 after being negative the prior week
failure_condition: If PARKS moves from negative to positive and RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines relative to the prior four-week mean over the next 28 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Higher RESIDENTIAL mobility reflects more time spent at home, which crowds out discretionary shopping trips and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated but RETAIL_REC does not fall within 7 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Retail mobility weakens when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are still deeply negative, because the city-center footfall base is too small to sustain nonessential shopping.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -20 and TRANSIT below -10 in the same week
failure_condition: If both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below the stated thresholds but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-2-week average within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A week-to-week rise in GROCERY_PHARM combined with flat or falling WORKPLACES marks a substitution toward essential errands and away from discretionary shopping, which should keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises while WORKPLACES does not recover and RETAIL_REC still exceeds its prior four-week mean within 28 days, reject the hypothesis.
